paragraphs.source_en: Indeed, Collins was participating in what she no doubt knew was a grand tradition that spanned generations and continents. Valentina Ponomareva, backup pilot to the first woman who ever went to space way back in 1963, said in an interview many years later that the women in the program had cheated on their medical exams. As she said, “the [male] cosmonauts of the first group treated us very well; they cared about us, they helped us, they taught us how to deceive physicians and how to pass tests easier.” Michael Collins, Moon-chauffeur to Armstrong and Aldrin, kept secret that he got claustrophobic in space suits, which he called “nasty little coffins,” even though he had to conduct spacewalks during missions. Nor have the years diminished the tradition.
